description: MATILDA is a Python model for water resources in glacierized catchments, developed by a cryosphere research team. It combines a temperature-index glacier melt component with HBV hydrology and provides parameter optimisation through SPOTPY. Inputs include temperature and precipitation, catchment and glacier parameters, and optional observed runoff; outputs are simulated melt, runoff and water-balance series. Coverage follows the chosen glacier basin and forcing period, with no fixed global grid. The MIT-licensed source is free, and the repository supplies example forcing and runoff files, installation instructions and a link to the wider MATILDA-Online workflow. Python 3.11 and several scientific libraries are required. A limitation is that a temperature-index melt scheme simplifies glacier energy balance, and results depend on local calibration and input elevation treatment. The model can inform reservoir inflow and drought simulations where glacier contribution matters. The catalogue's data-era5-reanalysis is a possible climate forcing source after downscaling checks, but no pairing was attempted here.
